favorite.name: Bavette's Bar & Boeuf
favorite.review: From the warm lighting, cozy ambiance to the the amount of care in presentation, taste, and balance in each dish here, this restaurant continues to be one of my favorite in all of Chicago. While you won’t go wrong with any dish on the menu, some of my favorites include the baked goat cheese, the smoked salmon caesar salad, and the fried (boneless) chicken. One thing that doesn’t nearly get enough attention on the menu is the burger. It’s truly exquisite. I recommend splitting it into halves or quarters to share, because it’s so rich but so delicious.

favorite.name: COTE Flatiron
favorite.review: After eating here I’m starting to understand the difference between a Korean bbq restaurant and a Korean steakhouse. As a korean bbq restaurant, you expect cheaper, marinated meats and to cook your own meats. But at a steakhouse, you’re eating much higher quality cuts of meat and they cook everything for you. So I think it’s not fair to really compare the two as they’re slightly different experiences… The beef tartare with caviar and milk bread was an extremely luxurious bite of food. The milk bread, caviar, and beef all took their individual flavors to the extreme. The caviar adds an excellent mouthfeel and juiciness, the milk bread has a richness and butteriness to it, and also so soft and pillowy. And the beef brings everything together and blends those flavors. It’s an appetizer you should order but it’s not really worth the value (such little food). The sides here were all excellent. Some of the best I’ve had, and comparable to the best you get in Korea in my opinion. 3 types of lettuce wraps/leaves to wrap meats, kimchi stews, etc. The meats themselves were great of course - tender, rich, juicy. The thing is when the sides are so good the meats don’t need to shine as much. The A5 wagyu was a treat to order, and obviously on another level compared to the other meats we got, but once again, you really pay for it. We paid such a premium, including drinks, appetizers, and the extra cuts of meat, and I’m not sure it’s worth ALL that value. If I were to come again, I’d just get the Butchers Feast per person. That’s worth the experience. Forget the add ons.

favorite.name: Von's 1000 Spirits
favorite.review: We ordered quintessential American food here - pizza, fries, and wings. Everything here has pretty good flavors. The sourdough pizza is doughy with a good chew, and the wings have a good sweet chili heat to them. The fries were the only dish that felt a little too heavy for me, the cheese was a little grainy and the pork and fries were good but ended up being a little heavy.

favorite.name: Ramsay's Kitchen
favorite.review: We got a reservation here a few months ago and we finally got the chance to try it yesterday. I’ve been to Hells Kitchen before so I’ll be comparing my experience to that. We got a round of cocktails, the tuna tartare and mushrooms for appetizers, the beef Wellington, salmon, and chicken Milanese for entrees, the Mac and cheese and carrots for sides, and finally the sticky toffee pudding for dessert. The cocktails were a little disappointing, I expected more flavor and interesting notes, though they were all balanced. The smoky whiskey cocktail was not smoky. The apps were really good, mushrooms especially. The beef Wellington was good but I think Hell’s Kitchen did it better. A little annoying to cut and eat properly and I think the beef was medium rare but just not as good as I was expecting. The other dishes were both superb though. The sides were great, certainly elevated with their own touch. Mac and cheese could have been even better but I was satisfied with it. The toffee pudding naturally blew away my party, rightfully so. The flavors go so well together and it’s a must order if you go. If I were to compare atmospheres, I liked Hells Kitchen more, it felt more special and unique. This felt a bit more generic to me.

favorite.name: HK Lounge Bistro
favorite.review: Great spot! The waiter was very nice and well spoken. The dumplings were awesome, especially the chive and shrimp ones. The sweet and sour pork was tender and crispy, though the sauce was not well distributed in the dish served to us. I should have gotten fried rice instead of the noodles as they looked a bit more appealing but what we got was still tasty.

favorite.name: Seastar Restaurant & Raw Bar
favorite.review: This was an excellent, excellent meal. Everything was prepared and served elegantly. We ordered the tower, salmon belly, deviled eggs, halibut ceviche, poke, and fries to start off. The tower included wonderful scallops and crab cakes - these were must haves. I’d recommend ordering just these to share; they were that good. The halibut ceviche and poke were also quite excellent. The fish was fresh and well flavored. The tortilla chips served with the ceviche were a little stale, but overall a minor nit in an otherwise excellent ensemble of appetizers. The truffle fries were shoestring fries, and honestly felt like frozen fries (not a bad thing). The sauces they came with were good, one was a truffle sauce and the other was ketchup. For the main appetizers, many in our party ordered the chilean sea bass and the scallops. Both dishes were superb; small portions and high prices but the meal was just very satisfying. In general, that was the theme of this entire meal - high prices, good food.

favorite.name: La Giostra
favorite.review: The reviews are right - get the pear ravioli and the florentine steak. Everything else is good but those two far outshine the rest. I really enjoyed the cozy atmosphere of this place. The free “bread” at the start of the meal was a very welcome and different surprise (the chicken liver bread was the best). The pear ravioli was light and airy but so creamy and flavorful. I liked the boar ragu pasta too quite a bit. The cacio e pepe was flavorful and rustic, not as white and creamy as others we’ve had. The seafood spicy pasta was not spicy but the seafood was enjoyable. The florentine steak looked almost medium rare even though we asked for rare but we really enjoyed it. Great crust, well seasoned, and mostly tender. Both the potato and sweet potatoes were absolutely excellent. Even though it may have been less authentic, we thought this was among the best we’ve had so far. I didn’t think either dessert (sache, tiramisu) was amazing but they were certainly tasty.

favorite.name: Pastéis de Belém
favorite.review: Place is worth the hype. It’s magical how large it is and how many people are moving in and out of this location. The egg custard tart was crispy, the custard hadn’t even set yet so it was very fresh. The textures were amazingly contrasting, the cinnamon and sugar sprinkled on top gave it more depth and flavor too. The eclair I was recommended was actually so tasty too - fresh cream and a hint of orange zest really added some freshness to the pastry. I came here alone so was limited to just two items. Would love to try everything on this menu!

favorite.name: Augustiner-Keller
favorite.review: Really large restaurant, excellent ambiance. The food was about average or slightly above average. I liked the potato dumpling here more than other places. Overall I recommend coming here.

favorite.name: Telefèric Barcelona Palo Alto
favorite.review: Excellent tapas! Loved the croquettes and the tuna tacos and the salmon tartare. Next time I’d like to try the beef dishes more.

favorite.name: Giano Restaurant
favorite.review: One of my favorite meals in Rome on our last night. This is a Sicilian restaurant for what it’s worth, so that might also explain the difference in flavors. Every dish was exquisite and used high quality ingredients. This felt like a Michelin star (or at least guide) restaurant to me. Both pasta dishes we ordered were the most popular and tasted great, the lamb was tender though not easy to split among 3 people. My favorite part of this meal was actually the desserts. The raspberry and fruit flavors really shined there and took the desserts to a whole other level. Don’t skip out on those.

favorite.name: Born and Bred
favorite.review: This is a very special dining experience. Hanwoo beef is not overrated, it’s a beefier Wagyu but also you don’t feel overwhelmed with the fat as much during the experience. (Eating too much probably still messes with your stomach). Everything being prepared and served for you is an even better dining experience. While it’s possible to get this experience in NYC maybe, the quality of the meats, the service, the authenticity of everything is hard to replicate. This is an absolute must eat in Seoul.

favorite.name: Fūunji
favorite.review: This dish has grown on me through my time in Japan. Dipping ramen has never been my favorite or go to, but Fuunji does it well. The spice mix they use keeps the broth interesting.

favorite.name: Bird Thais Restaurant
favorite.review: We got the papaya salad and spicy Thai fried rice - both were flavorful and good comfort food. Found the prices a little expensive for the portions.

favorite.name: The Hairy Lemon
favorite.review: Excellent chicken and puff pastry - the vibes were excellent and I loved the ambiance. The burgers didn’t look very good so stick to traditional Irish grub.

favorite.name: Incredible India Dubrovnik
favorite.review: For being the only Indian restaurant in Dubrovnik, this was pretty good. The garlic naan fell far below what we have in the US, but it still tastes good. Portions are small for what you’re paying but the Rogan Josh was really good, the lamb was tender.

favorite.name: Fig Hvar
favorite.review: Great flavors and plenty of food. The fig and cheese flatbread was a bit overhyped, it could have used some honey. I expected it to taste way better. I expected the Argentinian potatoes to be roast potatoes instead of fries. They were still tasty and I recommend ordering. The chicken burrito was a lot of food and sauced well. The owners were friendly Argentinians and we had a great time overall here.

favorite.name: Interstellar BBQ
favorite.review: Best BBQ I’ve had in my life - everything was to perfection. This is worth coming to and waiting an hour in line. Get here around 10:15. The sides are absolutely incredible - the Mac and cheese and coleslaw especially, but the scalloped potatoes too. We loved the duck, the pork belly, and pulled lamb.

favorite.name: Neptune Oyster
favorite.review: We got the 3 things I think were absolutely essential to try here: oysters, lobster roll, and johnnycakes. The oysters were amazing. I liked the ones with medium salt and a clear finish. We ordered one of the funkier ones and I didn’t like it quite as much. The lobster roll was 10 dollars more than Pauli’s next door but I’d say it was worth it. Slightly fresher lobster meat and the bread was highly elevated. The fries were a good addition too. The Johnny cakes though… wow. Extreme flavor bomb from the first bite. To be honest I’ve never heard of one before but the caviar, pate, and the syrup just made for such a wonderful flavor. I highly highly recommend ordering that. The best thing I had in Boston during my time here absolutely. Regarding getting into this restaurant, lining up at 10:30 is the move. I don’t think waiting here for 1.5 hours is worth it.

favorite.name: Satay
favorite.review: The chicken one and the pork DIY one were my favorite. The sampler looked cool but I didn’t care for most of them. Great little spot though.

favorite.name: Barrafina Dean Street
favorite.review: This was a bustling location, small and compact with bar seating to watch all the magic in the kitchen unfold before you. My favorites were the croquettes, the prawn tortilla, the bread with tomato, and the beef tenderloin. Everything is prepared with precision though and a certain quality that’s amazing to see.

favorite.name: Chocolatería San Ginés
favorite.review: The chocolate here is S tier - simply the best I’ve had, especially melted like this. This place is a chocolate place first, and churro place second. I enjoyed the churros but I think better exist. The fact that it’s open 24/7 is very impressive too.

favorite.name: Sabor a Peru
favorite.review: Authentic, no frills Peruvian food in Edgewater. I got the ceviche de pescado and there was a large quantity of food. Nothing to dip into the lime flavored liquid at the bottom of the bowl but I’m guessing that’s not traditional. The fish was very fresh. My friend got the fried fish with calamari. It was a super large portion of fried food. The calamari was okay, I’ve certainly had better. 5 stars for the overall quantity of food and the nonchalant atmosphere.

favorite.name: Milwaukee Brat House
favorite.review: Solid bratwurst and cheese curds! The buffalo sauce was not like Franks red hot and had a bit more complexity which was a good touch. The hot Hungarian sausage was the best of the 4 we tried. The food was surprisingly heavy so I’m glad we just ended up getting the sampler and the cheese curds. In our opinion those were the two dishes to get.

favorite.name: Doukato Restaurant
favorite.review: If I could rate this 6 stars I would. Every single dish was exquisite and among the best renditions of each dish I could have. The souvlaki is by far the star of the show. The meat is so tender and drips the meat juices over the potato. The meat is cooked perfectly, charred so well, and melts in your mouth. I could go through every single dish and tell you just how amazing it is, but my words wouldn’t do it justice. You should know that whatever you order, it will be prepared and cooked with the highest quality. I was with 3 Greeks who also vouched for how good every dish is comparable to the best restaurants in the villages. I don’t think I can describe just how amazing each dish is, this is probably the best tavern experience one can have. Do yourself a favor and get a reservation here.

favorite.name: JESTER Specialty Coffee & Juice
favorite.review: One of the more “American” places we visited during our time here, and it was actually pretty good. The coffee was better than other places and the açaí bowl was presented well.

favorite.name: Curry Hyuga
favorite.review: Hearty and delicious

favorite.name: The Front Door Pub
favorite.review: Excellent ambiance and experience - the gin flight was a lot of fun to order and it was fruity and floral. The prawns were good and the shepherds pie and beef and stew were cooked really well. I enjoyed the burger and the toffee pudding for dessert too! The sticky toffee pudding wasn’t as good as Ramsays rendition of it but it still is an excellent dessert you won’t be disappointed with. The place itself is a good ambiance with fun people, I recommend coming during your stay here.

favorite.name: La Voûte
favorite.review: A very unique, memorable night out. We started with a Japanese set course sushi menu (not super vegetarian friendly and half our party was vegetarian). Then the night slowly transformed into performances, magicians, dancers, and more. By 11:30 pm it became a full club and it was impressive to see the logistics of it all transform over the course of a few hours. Unique venue and worth a special occasion visit.

favorite.name: Moorings
favorite.review: We were astounded by the beauty of this restaurant. The incredible view overlooking the water, the marble top tables, and the clean, elegant black and white color palette throughout the entire space created a very professional, business, and polished ambiance. Since we had a large party of six, we decided to order a bit of everything from the menu. Each dish emphasized quality and presentation. Some of my favorites included the “crab rangoons” (shrimp filled with cheese), the spicy salmon sushi, the feta salad, the octopus, and the squid ink linguine. However, nearly everything we ordered was delicious. There was a good balance of Asian-inspired dishes like sushi and the “shrimp rangoon,” as well as Italian-inspired dishes like tiramisu and a few of the pastas. I also wanted to highlight the exceptional quality of the desserts. The tiramisu was exquisite, while the chocolate mousse and the fruit-flavored one were both very impressive. Each person in our group had a different favorite dessert. Is this the best value meal? No, but it’s an elite restaurant experience that’s meant to celebrate an occasion.

favorite.name: The Helmand
favorite.review: Awesome dining experience here. It felt like a home cooked meal. The standouts were definitely the rack of lamb (chowpan) and the pumpkin (which we got in the vegetarian special), but all the dishes had tremendous amounts of flavor and spices. The server was extra nice and managed to get us a a plate of mantwo even though it was sold out for the night. This place deserves the hype, go check it out!

favorite.name: Maize at the Station
favorite.review: The tacos really hold up. The tortillas taste great, thinly sliced ribeye with the melted cheese was great too. The free tortilla chips were thick but the salsa and all the dips are pretty addicting.

favorite.name: ARI Sushi Japanese Restaurant
favorite.review: I like the shumai, but I thought the sushi was overall expensive for what it is. Nice atmosphere though and certainly a hole in the wall!

favorite.name: Mausam
favorite.review: The view is excellent - wonderful outdoor terrace with a perfect view of the fountain and the buildings. The Delhi style butter chicken is pretty good, it had a nice char and smokiness to the curry. The naan was a bit disappointing and the chutney and samosas and grilled meats were also pretty solid.
favorite.address: Dubai Mall - Ground Level - Burj Khalifa - Downtown Dubai - Dubai - United Arab Emirates

favorite.name: Jack Stack Barbecue - Freight House
favorite.review: Truly incredible bbq - a step up from Joe’s. Joes has better sauce. But Jack Stack clears every other way. The sides are better (beans are comparable at both), the meats better, and you get significantly more food. We got Jacks Best for 4 and it’s an impressive amount of food, 3 people couldn’t finish it. The beef ribs are extremely fatty and tender and juicy - they are the best thing on the menu hands down. The pork ribs are also quite good, the sausage next, finally the burnt ends and lastly the beef brisket. Honestly, no point getting the beef brisket, the beef ribs are better in every way. I also really enjoyed the sides, and the pickles and the pickled onions to help cut the fat. The nicer ambiance and seating also help distinguish it from Joes. It isn’t much of a competition, if you had to pick one come to Jack Stack.

favorite.name: Kunjip Tofu
favorite.review: Excellent Korean food! I loved everything here, from the ambiance to the selection of curated dishes here. The ordering process was so simple and smooth, all of our food arrived in minutes of ordering but it was so fresh. The galbi, octopus bibimbap, and the seafood tofu soup were all so tremendous and was the perfect amount of food for two people. This review is simple because there’s not much to say - everything I ordered was delicious, prepared professionally and quickly, was clean and not oily, and very satisfying from start to end.

favorite.name: Sigi Ikthios
favorite.review: This was one of the best meals we had in Paros, so delicious that we had to return a second time to order the fish of the day again. However, I must mention that the restaurant is quite expensive. You can easily get carried away with tourist pricing and end up spending more than you intended. Despite this, I highly recommend trying the most expensive dishes - not the lobster, but the fish of the day and the special pasta of the day (the shrimp orzo, which costs 70 euros for four people). The star of the show is the fish of the day, a white fish cooked with butter and lemon sauce. It’s simply the best part of the meal, and the orzo is equally impressive. The tomato sauce in the shrimp orzo dish is incredibly fresh and honestly surpasses most pasta I’ve had in Italy. The restaurant staff also de-bones the fish and shrimp heads (if you order the special pasta, the shrimp orzo), making the meal much easier to enjoy. The ceviche, octopus (order it grilled, not the one on the menu), and mussels saganaki are all outstanding dishes that are definitely worth trying too. Another highlight is the tomato salad. The croutons here are among the most unique I’ve ever had. The restaurant also tends to offer free desserts. On both meals, we received the strawberry and cream puff pastry, which was a delightful way to end our meal before heading to the clubs.

favorite.name: Coneflower Creamery - Blackstone District
favorite.review: Amazing selection of ice cream. Butter brickle is incredible

favorite.name: Little Miss BBQ-Sunnyslope
favorite.review: Excellent food throughout. The beans were the best of the 3 sides, the Mac n cheese was creamy but the flavor a little off, and the grits congealed too quickly. The pastrami was fatty but the brisket was the star of the show. Shoutout to the pecan pie - the smoky flavor is incredible.

favorite.name: Fourtillfour Cafe
favorite.review: Excellent little shop. Great specials

favorite.name: BOKAMORRA HAUTE COUTURE PIZZA & COCKTAILS
favorite.review: Awesome vibes, music, and very tasty pizza. They even make very smooth cocktails. This was a good break from Croatian food. The meat pizza was my favorite though the caramelized onion one was pretty good too. And don’t skip out on the dessert pizza.

favorite.name: La Palapa
favorite.review: Writing this review for Sante - This was surprisingly a good meal! The salmon, the crab cakes and tuna tartare, and the soup were all indeed gourmet, and while my expectations were low for an all inclusive I had a good meal and would say it’s one of the better meals here.

favorite.name: Gallagher's Cork
favorite.review: Excellent place to stop by for lunch! The pie was well made - very hot but letting it crack open and mixing the ingredients helped bring it to an eating temperature. The meat was slow cooked and tender and flavored well. The cocktails were impressive, the fries were good, we liked the burgers too. The fish and chips look well portioned. Solid pub experience.

favorite.name: Big Pink
favorite.review: Really tasty, gluttonous American food. The chicken and waffles was cooked spectacularly, and the burger was thick but well put together. For such a large menu everything on the menu looked amazing.

favorite.name: A Thousand Tales Restaurant / Bakery & Cafe
favorite.review: Absolutely fantastic meal. Very crowded place, but accommodating to a larger party and earlier reservation. The mixed grill plate is extremely tasty, the meat is very well cooked. It was so tender that there was no Turkish sauces at all served with the plate, but I didn't mind that at all. The white rice is a great palette cleanser. This is hard to distinguish from a restaurant in Istanbul, which speaks volumes to the restaurant's authenticity. The fact that the restaurant doubles as a bakery with such a large assortment of pastries further enhances the experience. I'd love to go back a few times to explore all of the other things on the menu.

favorite.name: The Professor Döner
favorite.review: So far this is the perfect doner I’ve had - extremely juicy meat, crispy bread, and good moisture throughout. I just wish it was spicier

favorite.name: Anju
favorite.review: I thought this place was grossly overrated. I got the soju bourbon to start off, and just expected it to taste better than watered down soju. Then we got the dumplings and fried chicken and bone marrow as appetizers. The dumplings were great, and the fried chicken was cooked and sauced well but didn’t have a ton of spice. The bone marrow was decent, not a ton of food but good. Then we got the galbi and the pork tonkatsu - both meats were not the most tender. Disappointing for two main entrees.

favorite.name: Curry Hyuga
favorite.review: Excellent comfort food. I recommend the chicken katsu signature curry. It’s pretty filling, also I didn’t think the meenchi katsu is necessary to get. Also, love the number of ground spices, there’s a lot of variety!

favorite.name: Maranda Döner
favorite.review: I really enjoyed the fattiness and tenderness of the meat here. Do yourself a favor and come here.

favorite.name: PizzaExpress Daily
favorite.review: With the name of the spot I couldn’t tell butI was very surprised by the quality of this pizza. Fresh ingredients, well made. Would come back again!

favorite.name: L. Woods Tap & Pine Lodge
favorite.review: This is such an elevated, underrated American restaurant. All the food is just on another level. The free bread and fresh butter is not for everyone but I love the onion flavor. The wings are among the best they can be and I love how runny the blue cheese dip is. The steak skewers, Wagyu beef ribs, the steamed spinach and Mac and cheese were really good, I’d absolutely come back for any of those and have an excellent meal. I really enjoyed all the desserts too, the key lime pie and cookie skillet especially. Lovely restaurant and staff!

favorite.name: Osteria Papavero
favorite.review: Excellent authentic Italian place with rotating menu. I got the pork tenderloin and it was cooked to perfection. The bread basket was a little plain, wish it was served with butter or oil.

favorite.name: EZ Shawarma
favorite.review: This is an extremely satisfying chicken shawarma. For $9.99, you get a moist shawarma with sufficient amount of chicken. It’s wrapped so well, tastes fresh, and it’s traditional. Ask for the hot sauce. The only way it could be improved was if it had 10-15% more meat. But for this price point it’s certainly understandable.

favorite.name: Pizza Antica
favorite.review: Good chew of the bite. I liked the margherita the most actually. The other two needed a bit more sauce or chili oil. But this is classic, tasty Neapolitan pizza. Comes out quick.

favorite.name: P.F. Chang's
favorite.review: The honey chicken was actually my favorite thing here. Nothing was bad, it’s actually above average and better than you think. This is upscale chain Chinese food, and while you can get better elsewhere, a lot of it is quite tasty.

favorite.name: Chili Mac's Diner
favorite.review: Hidden gem diner in downtown St Louis. Awesome atmosphere and excellent food. Omelette and biscuits and gravy were above average and prices were so good!

favorite.name: Cafe Rose Red
favorite.review: One of my favorite restaurants in Bruges and even my time in Belgium - amazing tapas, especially the Indonesian chicken balls. We liked the potatoes and the dumplings a lot too. The drinks were great, great vibes, all around fantastic dining experience.

favorite.name: Toshi's Teriyaki
favorite.review: Great spot! I had to get the chicken and salmon teriyaki to try two things. The chicken katsu and spicy chicken looked tempting too, but I didn’t get to it this time. The salmon was flakey, the sauce was delicious, and the white rice was perfectly sticky. The chicken teriyaki was awesome too, though I expect the chicken katsu to be even better.

favorite.name: Tor Road Steak Aoyama
favorite.review: This is an excellent dining service with high quality ingredients.

favorite.name: Kama - La Grange
favorite.review: Solid food! We got a few drinks, snacks, and dessert. All the meat was tender, cooked fresh, and the naan tasted great too. Would come back again!

favorite.name: Avanzare Italian Restaurant - Lombard
favorite.review: The servers were really nice over here - attentive and polite. I thought the atmosphere was pretty quiet for a Sunday, and the food was good, but also average. The value was incredible - the 6 year anniversary menu was a lot of food for a very reasonable price. The beet salad was decent - the arugula was a little wilted and the beets could have been juicier, but I liked that there was plenty of goat cheese. The chicken was flavorful and there was plenty of veggies and potatoes. I liked the sausage more than the chicken. I didn’t care as much for the dish itself, and after ordering mussels with tomato sauce, I was a little tired of the tomato sauce. I think the pork chop (or a steak, or another pasta dish) would have been better to have for the 6 year anniversary menu. I really enjoyed the creme brulee though, there wasn’t a lot of custard but it came together well.

favorite.name: Hattie B's Hot Chicken - Nashville - Midtown
favorite.review: Really good Nashville hot chicken. Among the best. Presented really well too.

favorite.name: Papagalino's Cafe
favorite.review: Really nice interior, I felt like I was walking into a European cafe as soon as I entered! As many of the other reviews mentioned, parking here is tricky. I parked across the street and walked over. I just got a chocolate baklava and tea, but the baklava was fantastic. The desserts all looked excellent overall.

favorite.name: Bai Tong Thai Restaurant - Redmond
favorite.review: I was pretty disappointed with the crispy garlic chicken - chewy, overly crispy with not enough meat. Trusted the reviews on this one but I should have gone with my gut instinct and ordered a classic Thai dish. I think if I were to come back and get the Penang curry, I’d give it a higher rating

favorite.name: MAZRA
favorite.review: Great ambiance and selection of food - this felt more like a fast casual place to me but it was mostly comfort food. The dips were a miss, I didn’t think the halloumi cheese fries used really squeaky and savory halloumi cheese either. The meat, rice, and sauces it came with were good (the main meal) and I liked the fries. The rest of the food was a little forgettable. But overall this place has a good ambiance and easy ordering experience.

favorite.name: Moretti's Ristorante and Pizzeria
favorite.review: Pretty good spot! I enjoyed the chicken, it was well cooked and came well portioned. I would’ve loved to try the pizza.

favorite.name: Hakkai Nigiri Bar & Tapas
favorite.review: Absolutely incredible authentic hidden gem. Tremendous value, chefs choice 7pc for only 25 dollars is among the best I’ve found. And the fish is so high quality!

favorite.name: Mikiya Wagyu Shabu House | San Mateo
favorite.review: Very approachable hot pot. The wagyu is excellent, the broths are balanced and flavorful. The wagyu sushi is good, better than the bone marrow.

favorite.name: Simply South - Indian Vegetarian Restaurant
favorite.review: Good competition for A2B - I wish the dosa was a little crispier. The chutneys also taste a little bit worse than what you get at A2B Also, the chutneys, Dahl, and dosas can be definitely on the spicy side so be warned.

favorite.name: Kim's Uncle Pizza
favorite.review: The best of the best tavern style. This tavern style is cracker thin which is my favorite type of tavern. The sausage is fatty, large, and well cooked. The crust is addicting and the cheese is a bit wet when fresh out of the oven but letting it sit for a few minutes really helps.

favorite.name: Original Berliner Döner Würzburg
favorite.review: A beautiful combination of ingredients, textures, sauces, and flavors - I could eat this every day. The crispy texture of the bread is the first thing you taste, but you get the rest of the flavors quickly - the sauces (moisture), the juicy meat, and the pickled onions. The combination of everything just makes for an excellent, easily demolishable meal. All for just 8-9 euros. I understand now why this is the universal drunk food in Europe.

favorite.name: D16 Specialty Coffee Shop Zadar
favorite.review: Nice coffee , friendly staff
